newsitem.title: USA: Oral arguments in FDA tobacco appeal set August 11.
newsitem.headline: Oral arguments in FDA tobacco appeal set August 11.

text.p: A three-member federal appeals court will hear oral arguments August 11 on last spring's court decision upholding the Food and Drug Administration's (FDA) right to regulate of the U.S. tobacco industry.

An official of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fouth Circuit in Richmond, Virginia, said on Wednesday a written ruling would likely be issued several weeks after the arguments are made in Warm Springs, Virginia.
Federal Judge William Osteen last April ruled the FDA had the right to regulate the sale and labeling of cigarettes and other tobacco products but could not control their promotion and advertising.
Each side appealed the portion of Osteen's rulings that went against its interests.

The arguments, which are expected to take an hour to present, come against the backdrop of June's sweeping pact between state governments and tobacco companies covering, in part, government regulation of cigarettes. Approval of a deal by Congress and President Clinton is not expected until the autumn or later.

The FDA battle dates to August 1995, when Clinton authorized the agency to regulate cigarette sales and marketing. Some rules went into effect last winter and others are due to go into force next month.
